newsitem.title: POLAND: Good 96 CPI, EMU plans boost zloty to new highs.
newsitem.headline: Good 96 CPI, EMU plans boost zloty to new highs.

text.p: The Polish zloty climbed to new highs at 3.63/3.53 percent from the trading band centre -- the highest level since its one-off appreciation in December 1995 -- on foreign buying of treasury papers, dealers said.

They said foreigners sold about $50 million to buy Polish papers of nearly all maturities encouraged by better than expected 1996 inflation data and Poland's apparent will to enter the European Monetary Union (EMU) as early as 2004.
"There was strong currency selling against because foreigners started to buy Polish papers," said Konrad Kolasinski from American Bank in Poland (Amerbank).

"The good inflation data cut expectations of the central bank's nominal rate rise and Poland's EMU ambitions make its bonds attractive for longer-term foreign investors," a dealer at a foreign bank here said.
Year-on-year consumer inflation in 1996 dropped to 18.5 percent from 21.6 percent in 1995 against market expectations of about 18.8 percent.

The zloty firmed to 3.63/3.53 percent from the band centre, against Wednesday's 3.43/3.34 percent in busy trade. It closed at 2.9000/30 to the dollar, up from 2.9095/05 on Wednesday and at 1.8205/25 to the mark, down from 1.8215/25.
Dealers said that at today's 700 millon zloty fixed bond auction some 60 percent of the 518 million zlotys sold was likely to have been foreign bids.
Under the weight of high demand the yield of the benchmark 52-week T-bill fell 0.1 point to 19.80 percent against last Monday's primary auction average yield.

Some dealers expected that T-bill yields would still rise to match market rates driven up by the central bank to cool credit action, which doubled in 1996 in lending for households and rose more than 35 percent in corporate lending.

The central bank sold 91-day NBP-bills at 22.00 percent on Thursday against the last average 13-week T-bill yield of 19.47 percent and 182-day NBP-bills at 21.99 percent against 26-week T-bill yield of 19.61 percent.
But others said the large foreign demand would cap yields at around cut current levels.
"Foreigners with larger experience on the Polish market have already started to buy Polish paper... I expect yields will not go up any more," said Slawomir Soroczynski, T-bill dealer at BPH SA.
Overnight rates were flat on a balanced interbank deposit market at 21.25/21.65 percent against opening's 21.35/21.55 pct. Tomorrow/next were at 21.40/21.50 percent against 21.35/21.55 percent.
